Synopsis:
The player walks into the barracks room and disturbs a Flaming Fist who seems to be breaking into a locked chest. During conversation, the player can challenge him, discover the location of his stash, or attempt to persuade him not to flee, and to protect the city.The whole conversation should be in relatively low voice, as he doens't want to wake the others sleeping in the barracks.

Cluster Contexts:
- WYR_WyrmRock_BarracksGuard_003.json: The player has surprised a Flaming Fist corporal (Reynash) in a sleeping barracks while he’s covertly picking a lock; several comrades are asleep nearby so both characters keep their voices low to avoid waking them. Reynash is panicked and desperate — he claims to be quitting/deserting, mentions a wife at home and fears the approaching fighting and extortionate “danger money” at the docks, and will admit to hiding stolen goods on the roof if pressured. Off-screen, the city is tense (checkpoints and Steel Watchers are active nearby, refugees and rumors swirl), which helps explain his urge to flee. The scene supports player options to threaten him into surrendering the loot, learn the stash location, or try to persuade him to stay and protect the city.
- WYR_WyrmRock_BarracksInterrogation.json: This dialog happens when you encounter the Flaming Fist Thief in the Barracks area. If you wake the thief's colleagues his runs away and then one of the guards starts this dialog with you.

- WYR_RefugeeCamp_FlamingFist_001.json: A short dialog for the flaming fist guarding a back door of the Big Barn which holds donations for the refugees. Same dialog will be used in a case of this flaming fist catching the player inside the barn.

context: You surprised a Flaming Fist corporal (Reynash) in the sleeping barracks while he was covertly picking a comrade’s chest; both characters keep their voices low to avoid waking the other guards. Reynash is panicked and desperate—he claims to be quitting/deserting, frets about a wife at home, and complains about extortionate “danger money” at the docks as he plans to flee by ferry. Off-screen, the city is tense (checkpoints, Steel Watchers, refugees and rumors), which explains his urge to run and to hide stolen goods. If pressured he’ll admit the loot is stashed on the roof, but alerting others or letting him cry for help could draw his comrades; the player can threaten him, learn the stash location, or try to persuade him to stay and protect the city.
